questions.q: What does MIG (Multi-Instance GPU) provide that time-slicing does not?
options: Support on any NVIDIA GPU, regardless of age
Real hardware-level isolation, so one instance's workload cannot slow down or crash another
Unlimited subdivision of a GPU into any number of instances
The ability to combine multiple physical GPUs into one
questions.explain: MIG partitions a GPU at the hardware level into isolated instances, each with its own dedicated SMs, memory, and bandwidth. A workload on one instance cannot affect another instance on the same physical card.

options: Any NVIDIA GPU, including consumer cards
Only data-center GPUs like the A100 and H100
Only GPUs older than the Ampere architecture
MIG is a software-only feature that works on all GPUs
questions.explain: MIG is available on data-center GPUs like the A100 and H100, which have the hardware support needed for true partitioning.

questions.q: How does time-slicing share a GPU among multiple workloads?
options: It physically partitions the GPU's memory into separate isolated regions
It has the GPU's scheduler rapidly switch between workloads in time, with no memory isolation between them
It requires each workload to use a different physical GPU
It permanently reduces each workload's access to half the GPU's cores
questions.explain: Time-slicing lets workloads take turns using the full GPU's resources by rapidly switching between them, but all workloads share the same memory space with no isolation.

questions.q: What is a key risk of using time-slicing instead of MIG?
options: Time-slicing cannot be configured through Kubernetes at all
One workload can exhaust shared GPU memory or create contention that slows down every other workload on that card
Time-slicing requires A100 or H100 hardware specifically
Time-slicing permanently disables CUDA on the shared GPU
questions.explain: Because time-slicing provides no memory isolation, a misbehaving or resource-hungry workload can exhaust shared memory or create contention that degrades performance for every other workload sharing that GPU.

questions.q: In the time-slicing device plugin config example, what does `replicas: 4` accomplish?
options: It physically creates 4 separate GPUs from one card
It makes Kubernetes advertise 4 schedulable nvidia.com/gpu slots on a single physical GPU
It limits the GPU to a maximum of 4 CUDA streams
It quadruples the GPU's available memory
questions.explain: Setting replicas: 4 in the device plugin's time-slicing config makes Kubernetes advertise 4 schedulable "GPU" resources backed by the same single physical card, allowing up to 4 workloads to be scheduled onto it.
